dastgahCycle.caption: Step through the cyclic architecture of a Dastgāh: opening in the Mother Maqām (Darāmad), modulating through secondary Maqāms in higher registers, and returning home via the Forūd.

stages.title: Darāmad (درآمد)
stages.description: Introduces the mother maqām in the lower/middle register, establishing the home tonal center and primary modal ethos.

stages.title: Secondary Gūsheh I
stages.description: Shifts the focal degree upward into a related secondary maqām, introducing fresh modal color while remaining connected to the parent system.

stages.title: High-Register Gūsheh (Owj)
stages.description: Reaches the upper register (e.g., Delkash or Erāq in Māhūr), maximizing emotional intensity and modal distance from the Darāmad.

stages.title: Forūd (فرود)
stages.description: A recognizable cadential melodic model (sarmashq) that descends back to the mother maqām's finalis, closing the modal cycle smoothly.

forudMahur.caption: Interactive cadential model of a classic Forūd-e Māhūr: stepwise descent through the lower dāng, lower neighbor dip to B3, and resolution to C4.

dastgahTree.caption: Explore the 7 canonical Dastgāhs and 5 derived Āvāzes (12 modal branches) of Persian classical music.

dastgahs.name: Shūr
dastgahs.note: The largest branch of the Persian modal system, giving rise to four of the five canonical Āvāzes (plus Bayāt-e Kord in some classifications).

dastgahs.name: Navā
dastgahs.note: Independent Dastgāh with no canonical derived Āvāzes; deeply linked to the Shūr modal family in tuning and ethos.

dastgahs.name: Segāh
dastgahs.note: Independent Dastgāh anchored on a neutral (koron) tonic, featuring major modally specific gūshehs such as Zābol and Mokhālef.

dastgahs.name: Chahārgāh
dastgahs.note: Independent Dastgāh characterized by symmetrical neutral-interval tetrachords and prominent gūshehs like Zābol, Mokhālef, and Ḥeṣār.

dastgahs.name: Homāyūn
dastgahs.note: Parent Dastgāh of the fifth canonical Āvāz, Bayāt-e Eṣfahān; also houses expansive gūshehs such as Shūshtarī.

dastgahs.name: Māhūr
dastgahs.note: Independent Dastgāh renowned for wide-ranging modulations (e.g., Delkash, Erāq) unified by its unmistakable Forūd-e Māhūr.

dastgahs.name: Rāst-Panjgāh
dastgahs.note: Independent Dastgāh that shares Māhūr's basic scale foundation while traversing an unusually broad set of modulations across other dastgāhs.
